transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump has announced that Stephen Miller will be the next White House Chief of Staff,
replacing Suzy Wiles, who's currently in the role.
Stephen Miller will be the new Chief of Staff, and Suzy's going to go over to the political operation.
What do you want? What do you want, Stephen Miller?
Just run things well.
Shelby Talcott is a White House correspondent for semaphore.
She tells NPR that President Trump blamed Wiles for the blistering Republican losses in the midterms.
The president effectively blamed Suzy Wiles for that performance,
and while he didn't overtly ask for her resignation,
he was angry at her earlier this week, and on Thursday night she told him,
"Let me make this easy on you. I'm going to resign."
Stephen Miller has been one of the architects of the president's most hardline immigration policies.
In a social media post, Trump called Miller one of his most trusted advisers.
Two U.S. Senate races are still too close to call.
NPR's Ashley Lopez reports election officials in Mississippi and Alaska continue to count ballots three days after the midterms.
Both Alaska and Mississippi have closely watched Senate races that are coming down to very slim margins.
As of Friday at last check, Alaska's Senate race between Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan
and Democrat Mary Peltola was down to a margin of several hundred votes.
And because the races are so close, every ballot counts at this point.
Both states accept postmark late arriving mail ballots, so not all ballots are even at election offices.
Because of the margins, many of those ballots will need to be counted before a race call is likely,
and Mississippi election officials are also working through quite a few provisional ballots.
Those are typically given to voters who face questions about their eligibility at the polls.
Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
Tesla says it will wind down production of its Cybertruck in Texas next year.
NPR's Willa Rubin reports the sales have struggled since the vehicle went on sale in 2023.
The Cybertruck was divisive from the get-go.
The electric pickup truck has a brutalist, boxy design that people either love, hate, or love to hate.
Production began in 2023, but the model has been plagued by recalls, and by not many sales.
In Musk's announcement on X, he says Tesla's making more room in its Texas Gigafactory to instead build cybercabs, a robo-taxi.
On the company's most recent earnings call, Musk reiterated that his vision for Tesla's feature includes robo-taxis and even humanoid robots.
Tesla discontinued its pricier car models, the Model S and the Model X, earlier this year.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs last month. That's far more than economists had expected.
This is NPR News.
Former West Virginia Senator John D. Rockefeller IV has died at the age of 89.
The Democrats served two terms as governor and spent 30 years in the U.S. Senate.
In Congress, he pushed to expand health coverage for low-income Americans.
Archaeologists have found the earliest evidence of humans using cannabis to get high almost 3,000 years ago.
NPR's Nate Rodd reports.
Scythians were a nomadic people that roamed the Eurasian steppes.
And almost a decade ago, archaeologists found a massive burial mound that they made in current-day Siberia.
In it, the scientists found intact cannabis seeds and human hair from a person who lived 2,800 years ago.
They ran a drug test on the hair, because why not?
And in a new paper published in the journal Science, the archaeologists say it tested positive for THC, the psychoactive compound in cannabis.
Researchers warn that doesn't mean the people were intentionally smoking it for the buzz, but if so, it suggests humans have been using the plant far longer than previously believed.
Nate Rodd, NPR News.
A rare dinosaur fossil from France is heading to auction, and some scientists are worried about who buys it.
It includes one of the best-preserved skulls ever discovered from that group of dinosaurs.
Researchers worry that if it goes into a private collection, they could lose access to it.
At last check on Wall Street, the Dow was down 237 points.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump names Stephen Miller next White House Chief of Staff, replacing Suzy Wiles
Mississippi and Alaska Senate races remain too close to call as ballots are counted
Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas next year, shifting space to robotaxis
U.S. employers add 165,000 jobs last month, far above economists' expectations
Former West Virginia Senator John D. Rockefeller IV dies at age 89
Archaeologists find THC in 2,800-year-old Scythian hair, earliest evidence of cannabis use
Rare French dinosaur fossil, including a well-preserved skull, headed to auction
Dow falls 237 points in late trading on Wall Street
